All the code used in testing is open source and available on [GitLab](https://c212.net/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=2508835-1&h=287797929&u=https%3A%2F%2Fgitlab.com%2Fongresinc%2Fbenchplatform&a=GitLab) so others can independently reproduce and audit the results. "The benchmark was designed to be reproducible and run on a public cloud, so anyone who wants to compare Postgres and MongoDB can easily do so," said Alvaro Hernandez, founder of OnGres. "We're sharing all the information on the tests we ran, why they were selected and the results we found so that anyone can reproduce the results or change parameters and configurations for their own needs."

The GitLab project includes two repositories which allow a comparison of the performance of Postgres 11.1 and MongoDB 4.0 running on Amazon Web Services (AWS). The goal of the benchmark was to compare the performance of Postgres and MongoDB in several different use cases while simulating real-life production scenarios as much as possible. The tests analyze the capabilities and performance of Postgres and MongoDB using the same data design across a range of active dataset sizes. Both public and generated datasets were used.
